question: Why does no confusion of cognitions arise despite an undivided group of knowers?
premises: The group of knowers remains undivided even in diverse cognitions.
Cognitions are connected with distinct modes of manifestation.
Distinct manifestation prevents the mixing of cognitions.
inference: Therefore no confusion of cognitions occurs even though the knowers are undivided.
plain_english: Even though the group of knowing subjects is undivided, there is no confusion of cognitions, because each cognition arises through its own distinct mode of manifestation.
